2. API-NAMPA CONSERVATION AREA
Area
Established : 2010
Location : Darchula
Features:
i.Api-nampa conservation area is named after the peaks Api and Nampa.
ii.Its altitude ranges from 539 to 7,132 m.
iii.It was established to conserve the unique flora, fauna, biodiversity and cultural heritage of the
area.
iv.Its altitude variation offers diverse climatic condition supporting several wildlife including
mammals like Himalayan Tahr, Blue sheep, Musk deer, common langur (Semnopithecus
entellus), jackal (Canis aureus), grey wolf (Canis lupus) (V), Himalayan black bear
(Selenarctos thibetanus) (V), Red panda (Ailurus fulgens) (V), snow leopard (Uncia uncia)
(E), Himalayan musk deer (Moschus chrysogaster), Serow (Capricornis sumatraensis) (I),
Himalayan tahr (Hemitragus jemlahicus) (K) and goral (Nemorhaedus goral).
v.Some major species of bird it accommodates include Daphne (Impeyan pheasant), Munal,
Snow Chock, Blood pheasant, Red billed chough, Yellow-billed chough, etc.
vi.It is also famous for valuable medicinal Panchaunle (Dactylorhiza hatagirea), Kutki
(Neopicrorhiza scrophulariiflora), Yarsagumbu (Cordyceps sinensis), Jatamansi
(Nardostachys grandiflora), Sarpagandha (Rauvolfia serpentina), Sugandhawal (Valeriana
jatamansi), etc.
3. GAURISHANKAR CONSERVATION AREA
Area
Established : January 2010
Location : Ramechhap, Dolakha and Sindhupalchok
Features:
i. The Nepal Government gave the National Trust for Nature Conservation (NTNC) the
job of managing the Gaurishankar Conservation Area for 20 years.
ii. It is primarily rich in 16 types of vegetations: Pinus roxburghii forest, Schima-
Castanopsis forest, Alnus forest, Pinus wallichiana forest, Pinus patula forest,
Rhododendron forest, Quercus lanata forest, Lower temperate oak forest (Quercus
semicarpifolia forest), Lower temperate mixed broad leaved forest, Abies forest, Upper
temperate mixed forest (Birch-rhododendron forest), Temperate mountain oak forest,
East Himalayan Oak forest, Juniperus forest, Shrubland (Rhododendron anthopogon
bushes) and Moist alpine scrubs.
iii. Forest and bushes, cultivated land, grasslands and glaciers occupy 44.5%, 8.8%, 8.6%,
and 2.77% of the total area, respectively.
iv. It harbors 565 species of plants, 77 species of mammals, 16 species of fishes, 9 species
of amphibians, 22 species of reptiles and 235 species of birds.
